newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bankgesellschaft, NordLB get go-ahead for talks.
newsitem.headline: Bankgesellschaft, NordLB get go-ahead for talks.

text.p: Bankgesellschaft Berlin AG and Norddeutsche Landesbank, two state-owned German banks regarded by analysts as candidates for possible merger, said on Monday they would intensify talks about cooperating more closely.

In a joint statement, the banks said their owners, several regional governments in northern and eastern Germany, had on Friday reviewed management proposals for closer cooperation and instructed the chief executives to enter closer talks.
But it was unclear whether these proposals envisaged the purchase of cross shareholdings or even a full merger.
Bankgesellschaft said in June a takeover of NordLB would be a feasible way to strengthen existing cooperation, but NordLB quickly retorted that such a step was highly unlikely.

"Talks are at such an early stage that the only thing that is really definite now is that the politicians have said they support it," a Bankgesellschaft spokeswoman said in response to a Reuter enquiry on Monday.
"There are no decisions in any direction," the spokeswoman said. She said she could give no details of the proposals.
A merger would create one of Germany's biggest banks with a combined balance sheet total of roughly 480 billion marks ($315.1 billion).
The two banks already cooperate in economic research and have set up a joint venture to develop software for them.

NordLB is majority-owned by the states of Lower Saxony, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and Saxony-Anhalt as well as by regional savings banks associations. Bankgesellschaft is 56 percent owned by the state of Berlin.
NordLB, a regional bank which acts as clearing bank to the savings banks in the states that own it, holds a stake just under 20 percent in Bankgesellschaft.

NordLB chief executive Manfred Bodin said recently a merger would be extremely difficult for legal reasons because Bankgesellschaft had the status of a shareholding company under private law and NordLB was a regional bank under public law.

Analysts have said several big German banks will eventually have to contemplate mergers to rationalise their inefficient branch networks and gain the critical mass needed to survive fierce competiotion after European monetary union.
The speculation heated up after Germany's largest commercial bank, Deutsche Bank AG, announced in July it had amassed a 5.21 percent stake in Bayerische Vereinsbank AG.
Deutsche has said the stake was intended to deter potential bidders and that it had no immediate plans to increase the stake.
